newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Telrad buys shares in parent Koor.
newsitem.headline: Telrad buys shares in parent Koor.

text.p: Telecommunications company Telrad has begun to buy shares through the bourse in its parent company Koor Industries, Israel's largest holding concern, Koor said on Wednesday.
In the first purchase on September 2 Telrad bought 7,215 shares, or 0.05 percent of the voting rights, for about two million shekels.
Telrad will continue to purchase Koor shares from time to time on the bourse and will hold these shares for at least three months.
Israeli companies by law are prohibited from buying their own shares but subsidiaries may buy shares in their parent companies.
Telrad is wholly owned by Koor, which is also listed in New York.
